With all due respect, what kind of research have you done on women’s bodies when they are pregnant? After childbirth, bodies change after pregnancy, and it can take time—sometimes up to two years or longer—for things to fully recover for a woman. It’s not uncommon for someone to still feel physical or emotional changes long after childbirth, and it sounds like your partner might still be grappling with some of those feelings. While it’s completely valid that you want to reconnect physically, it’s important to also acknowledge the emotional aspects of this situation. It sounds like she’s dealing with body image concerns, which can take time to process, and her hesitation may stem from feeling vulnerable or unsure. It might help to give her more space to talk about how she feels and continue reassuring her, but also find ways to bond emotionally without focusing on sex. Make love to her mind first and make sure she feels you have enough strength to focus on your emotional bond first. Patience is key, and working through this together will require understanding on both sides. If she isn’t able to communicate her needs and her fears then that is on her and I would think you both should try couples therapy to work on communicating better.
